Notice that the given series is a geometric series because it is in the form $\sum a{r}^{n}.$ 

The sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of a geometric series is given by the formula

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1,
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term and $r$ is the common ratio.

The first term is

$$
{a}_{1}=10{(\frac{1}{2})}^{1}=5.
$$

 

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{10{(\frac{1}{2})}^{2}}{10{(\frac{1}{2})}^{1}}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }10{(\frac{1}{2})}^{n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{5}{(1-\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =\frac{5}{(\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =5\cdot \frac{2}{1} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the first term is ${a}_{3},$ and so the sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of this geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{3}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

For the first few terms, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3} & =\frac{4}{9}{(\frac{3}{4})}^{3}=\frac{4}{9}(\frac{27}{64})=\frac{3}{16} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{4}{9}{(\frac{3}{4})}^{4}=\frac{4}{9}(\frac{81}{256})=\frac{9}{64}\end{aligned}
$$

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{4}}{{a}_{3}}=\frac{(\frac{9}{64})}{(\frac{3}{16})}=\frac{9}{64}\cdot \frac{16}{3}=\frac{3}{4}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=3}^{\infty }\frac{4}{9}{(\frac{3}{4})}^{n} & =\frac{{a}_{3}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{16})}{(1-\frac{3}{4})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{16})}{(\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{3}{16}\cdot 4 \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

The first term is 

$$
{a}_{1}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2(1)}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}
$$

 

and the second term is 

$$
{a}_{2}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2(2)}=\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{4}.
$$

Therefore, the common ratio is 

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{4}}{\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}={(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}.
$$

 

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{9}{4}{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2n} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{\frac{9}{4}(\frac{1}{9})}{(1-\frac{1}{9})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{4})}{(\frac{8}{9})} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{9}{8} \\  & =\frac{9}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$
